claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Cube Core is an open-source semantic layer; users define metrics, dimensions, joins, and access rules once in code and expose them via SQL, REST, and GraphQL APIs to BI tools, custom applications, or AI agents.
claims.quote: **Cube Core is the open-source semantic layer.** Define metrics, dimensions, joins, and access rules once in code, then expose them through SQL, REST, and GraphQL APIs to anything downstream — BI tools, custom applications, or AI agents.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The source defines a semantic layer as the core engine of BI tools that defines metrics, dimensions, and business logic and hides underlying data source complexity.
claims.quote: Every BI tool relies on a semantic layer as its core engine — the component that defines metrics, dimensions, and business logic and hides the complexity of the underlying data sources.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The source contrasts most semantic layers as proprietary and single-BI-coupled with Cube Core as an open standalone semantic layer consumable by analytics applications or AI agents via standard APIs.
claims.quote: Most semantic layers are proprietary, tightly coupled to a single BI platform, and can't be reused across other tools. Cube Core is an open, standalone semantic layer that any analytics application or AI agent can consume through standard APIs.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Cube says metrics defined once can be used across internal BI, embedded analytics, and AI agents without reimplementing the model in each place.
claims.quote: Define your metrics once and use them everywhere — internal BI, embedded analytics, AI agents — without re-implementing the model in each place.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Cube Core supports all SQL data sources, naming Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Presto, Amazon Athena, and Postgres.
claims.quote: Cube Core works with all SQL data sources, including cloud data warehouses like Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery; query engines like Presto and Amazon Athena; and application databases like Postgres.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Cube Core includes a built-in relational caching engine intended to provide sub-second latency and high concurrency for API requests.
claims.quote: It has a built-in relational caching engine to provide sub-second latency and high concurrency for API requests.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Cube Core and the commercial Cube product share a fully compatible data model in both directions.
claims.quote: The data model is fully compatible both ways: a model you build in Cube Core runs unchanged in Cube, and vice versa.
